grammar.label: whether vs if, and embedded questions in formal writing
grammar.form: whether (or not) + clause; whether + to-infinitive; question word + statement order
grammar.meaning: reports a question without asking it

explanation.en: 'Whether' works everywhere 'if' does, and in places 'if' cannot: after a preposition ('the question of whether'), before a to-infinitive ('whether to accept'), and with 'or not' attached. An embedded question keeps statement word order: 'I asked where the file was', not 'where was the file'.
explanation.uz: 'whether' 'if' o'rniga har doim ishlatiladi va qo'shimcha o'rinlari bor: predlogdan keyin, 'to' dan oldin va 'or not' bilan. Ergashgan savolda so'z tartibi darak gapnikidek qoladi.

grammar.positive_example: The letter asks whether the deadline can be extended.
grammar.negative_example: The letter asks if or not can the deadline be extended.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek va rus tillarida ergashgan savolda so'z tartibi o'zgarmagani uchun ingliz tilida ham savol tartibi saqlanib qolishi tez-tez uchraydi.

grammar.label: negative and rhetorical questions
grammar.form: Isn't it…? / Don't you think…? / Who would have thought…?
grammar.meaning: expects agreement, or makes a statement in question form

explanation.en: A negative question usually invites agreement: 'Isn't that expensive?' expects 'Yes'. A rhetorical question asserts rather than asks: 'Who could possibly object?' means nobody could. Answering 'yes' or 'no' to an English negative question follows the fact, not the question's polarity.
explanation.uz: Inkor savoli odatda rozilik kutadi. Ritorik savol javob so'ramaydi, balki fikrni bildiradi. Ingliz tilida inkor savoliga javob savolning shakliga emas, faktga qarab beriladi.

grammar.positive_example: Don't you think we should ask them first?
grammar.negative_example: Don't you think we should not ask them first, do you?

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek va rus tillarida inkor savoliga 'ha' deb javob berish inkorni tasdiqlaydi; ingliz tilida esa 'yes' doim ijobiy faktni bildiradi — bu jiddiy tushunmovchilik manbai.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I have written 'I want to know if you will extend the deadline'.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: In a letter, 'whether'. And they did not ask what you want; they asked what you need.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'I am writing to enquire whether the deadline can be extended.'

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Better. Notice you kept statement order — not 'whether can the deadline be extended'.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Everybody nearly writes that. Now the second paragraph.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'Don't you think two weeks is reasonable?'

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: That is a question you would ask a colleague, not a registrar.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: State it, and let them disagree if they wish. A question that expects agreement can read as pressure.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'Should you require further information, please write.'

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Now it sounds like somebody they will answer.
